_comment: Run template for lbnl-b59 (a real office without DCV). Equipment: the four rooftop units (AHU; RTU0N), the 11 CO2 zones (VAV; RTU0N_zone_<z>) and, in the full subset, the 51 underfloor fan terminals (VAV; RTU0N_uft_<z>). dcv_system_verification joins each zone's CO2 to its RTU's measured OA flow through the RTU0N_ name prefix (a heuristic grouping built from the Brick model, so severities are capped at warn); OA flow is masked before 2020-04-10, so OA-flow verdicts come from April-December 2020. oa_floor_cfm 750 is the 62.1 area component Ra*Az = 0.06 cfm/ft2 x 12,513 ft2 -- the two 2,325 m2 office floors split evenly over the four RTUs, an ASSUMPTION because per-RTU areas are not published (the descriptor's 5,000 cfm is the RTU design minimum OA, not a 62.1 floor). The building has no economizer command point and a mild climate, so the rule infers the economizer from OAT and is expected to decline ('not judged') rather than call DCV functioning -- the specificity lesson. unmet_setpoint_hours runs on the terminals of the full subset. Not run: co2_ventilation (zone CO2 medians are 419-429 ppm in both years, so it reads 'over-ventilated, energy opportunity' on every zone -- but this OA comes from an economizer in a mild climate, which cools for free; the rule does not know that), outdoor_air_fraction (no trustworthy unit minimum: the OA/supply flow ratio at the 10% minimum damper is 7-19% and the temperature balance 2-17% by unit, while the design minimum is 25%, and the mixed-air sensors are doubtful -- see the data issues), ventilation_rate_62_1 (per-RTU areas and populations are not published; issue #17), and the drift families (no labelled baseline period).
